# The Problem

Clinical prediction models that perform well in their development data may perform differently across populations, institutions, countries and time periods because of differences in case mix, measurement practices, treatment pathways and outcome prevalence [@riley2016; @collins2015]. Multisite external validation is therefore important for assessing transportability and heterogeneity in model performance.

Conventional pooled validation requires patient-level records to be transferred to a central location, which may be restricted by governance, ethical, legal or operational requirements. Federated analysis offers an alternative by retaining records locally, but participating sites must still implement consistent cohort definitions, predictor transformations, model equations, missing-data rules, performance measures and output controls. These challenges particularly affect clinical and public-health researchers, registry networks and data custodians coordinating validation across heterogeneous or resource-constrained settings.

Existing approaches address parts of this problem. DataSHIELD provides distributed analysis with client-server infrastructure and disclosure controls, including tools for assessing model performance [@gaye2014], while OHDSI PatientLevelPrediction supports reproducible network studies using data mapped to the OMOP Common Data Model [@reps2018]. Other R packages provide established methods for performance estimation and evidence synthesis. However, a practical gap remains for networks whose sites can run R but cannot deploy persistent federated servers or transform entire databases to a common data model. **fedvalidateR** will address this gap by providing a lightweight, study-specific protocol-to-report workflow for local mapping, data-quality checks, model validation, reviewable aggregate outputs and cross-site synthesis. It is intended to complement, rather than replace, existing federated platforms.
